tasks.title: Make evidence revocation and restoration safe and replay-consistent
tasks.description: In orchestrator/creator_dna/store.py, separate creator rejection from attribution revocation. Today revoke_attribution() and reject_evidence() both write evidence_review/reject, _apply() treats every action other than reject as a restore, and restore_evidence() can make evidence from a withdrawn attribution eligible again (also after replay); a revocation of already creator-rejected evidence is not recorded at all. Fix: independent creator_rejected and attribution_revoked state with rejected kept as a read-only compatibility property; a distinct attribution_revoked event (decision ID and reason, schema v4); strict evidence_review actions (reject, restore only); restore clears only creator rejection and is refused for revoked or flagged possible-legacy-revoked evidence; revocation is recorded even for creator-rejected evidence and is idempotent per decision. Legacy v1-v3 logs replay with their original semantics; a note-prefix heuristic may only set read-only warning flags. Synthetic regression tests and a documentation update. No change to speaker_attribution/ or any cross-package test; no real footage.
acceptance_criteria: Creator rejection and attribution revocation are independent state; EvidenceItem.rejected stays a read-only property true for either, and existing readers of rejected and review_note are unchanged
Revocation is written as a distinct attribution_revoked event with decision ID and reason (schema v4); evidence_review accepts only reject and restore and any other action fails replay
restore_evidence clears only creator rejection, never undoes a current revocation, and is refused for revoked evidence and for evidence flagged as a possible legacy revocation
revoke_attribution records a revocation for creator-rejected evidence; repeated revoke_attribution/sync_revocations for the same decision emit no new events
Legacy v1-v3 logs replay with original semantics; ambiguous historical rejects are only flagged (read-only warnings), never migrated or reinterpreted
Exports keep rejected_by_creator creator-specific and expose attribution revocation, decision ID and reason separately

Synthetic regression tests cover revoke then restore, creator reject then revoke, unknown actions, reload/replay equivalence, repeated synchronization and legacy replay/reporting; test_speaker_attribution.py passes unmodified
CREATOR_DNA.md documents the event model, legacy handling and restore rules; the full suite passes with python -B -I

tasks.title: Asset acquisition pipeline and rights-evidence handling (offline, transport-injected)
tasks.description: Wave w01-acquisition-providers-review, lane L1: Asset acquisition pipeline and rights-evidence handling (offline, transport-injected).
acceptance_criteria: A new module orchestrator/assets/acquisition.py provides an explicit acquire step: it runs the existing triage/rights decision first, fetches only PERMITTED candidates, records QUARANTINE candidates as quarantined records with their reason codes and never fetches them, and never fetches REJECT candidates; unknown rights are never permission

Fetching goes through an injected Transport protocol (no real network code is exercised anywhere): https-only URLs, a per-provider host allow-list, a maximum byte size, a content-type allow-list per media type, a timeout parameter; the file is written atomically (temporary file, sha256 verified, then moved into the library layout), refuses path traversal, never overwrites an existing asset, and detects duplicates by sha256

Every failure path (transport error, truncated or oversize download, wrong content type, hash mismatch, library write error) leaves no partial file behind and records a scrubbed error that contains no credential-like text; each path has its own test

Rights-evidence handling: the licence evidence captured at acquisition (source URL, retrieval date, a hash of the licence text snapshot, the verifier) is stored with the asset; a re-verification function detects licence drift (stored hash differs from the current text) and moves the asset to quarantine without deleting it; human attestations keep working through the existing Attestation model

A concrete offline LocalFolderProvider searches a directory of user-supplied files described by sidecar rights files (documented, validated schema, strict: unknown keys and missing rights are quarantined, never permitted); acquisition copies, and original files are never modified, moved or deleted (a test hashes the originals before and after)

At least one open-licence catalogue adapter (Openverse or Wikimedia Commons) is implemented as a pure request builder plus response parser over the injected transport and tested only against fixture payloads authored from the public API documentation; the documentation and the report state NOT TESTED against the live service

A single function find_and_acquire(request, registry, library, transport, context) runs search, triage and acquisition and returns a deterministic report listing acquired, quarantined, rejected and failed items with reasons; ordering is stable across runs

At least 60 new offline tests in orchestrator/tests/test_asset_acquisition.py; one test proves no network is touched (socket creation is patched to fail); synthetic tiny files only, no real media; the existing test_assets.py passes (it may be extended, never weakened)

ASSETS.md documents the acquisition flow, the sidecar schema, the failure behaviour and what is IMPLEMENTED versus NOT TESTED (live providers, real media); open questions are listed, not decided; the lane report lists anything needing a decision from Lukas
